texts.r:skill:e.e1.alpha: Words easy to remember when you know di first sound and first letter. Say di sounds out loud as you read.
texts.r:skill:e.e1.greet: When you meet somebody, say **Hello**. When you leave, say **Goodbye**. Say your name with **My name is ...**.
texts.r:skill:e.e1.numcol: Learn number words like one, two, three... and color words like red, blue, yellow...
texts.r:skill:e.e1.family: Mother (mum), father (dad), grandmother (grandma), baby (very small child): these are words for people in your family.
texts.r:skill:e.e1.class: Desk, chair, bag, pencil, book... Say di things for your classroom in English.
texts.r:skill:e.e2.noun: Words wey name things, like rabbit (animal with long ears), bird (animal wey fly), and fish (animal wey swim), dem dey call **nouns**.
texts.r:skill:e.e2.verb: Words wey show action, like jump (go up in di air), run (move fast), and eat (chop food), dem dey call **verbs**.
texts.r:skill:e.e2.like: **I like ...** mean say you enjoy something. **I have ...** mean say something belong to you.
texts.r:skill:e.e2.sent: After I, use **am**. After You, use **are**. Sentence order na: “who → wetin dem be / wetin dem do”.
texts.r:skill:e.e2.read: When you read, first find words from di question inside di text.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.build: Put sentence parts in dis order: “who → do → wetin”. After He, She, or person name, add **-s** to verb.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.pron: Instead of name, you fit use **He**, **She**, **It**, **They**, or **We**.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.tense: For something wey dey happen now or again and again, use **present tense**. For wetin don happen, use **past tense**: add **-ed** to end of verb.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.routine: wake up, brush my teeth, chop breakfast, go sleep... Talk about your daily routine in English.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.read: Read di text and find who do wetin and when.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.abc1: Alphabet get **capital letters** and **small letters**. Many letter pairs look different, so learn dem one pair at a time. Watch letters wey look alike, like b, d, p and q.
texts.r:skill:e.e3.snd1: First sound of a word connect with its first letter. Find words wey start with same sound to learn how sound and spelling relate. Sometimes two letters, like ph, make f sound.
texts.r:skill:e.e4.tense: For now or habits, use **present tense**. For past, add **-ed**. For wetin you go do, use **will + base verb**.
texts.r:skill:e.e4.qneg: Start question with **Do/Does**. To say no, use **don't/doesn't**.
texts.r:skill:e.e4.adj: Words like big, small, hot, and cold describe how something look or feel.
texts.r:skill:e.e4.prep: Use **on**, **in**, **under**, and **behind** to talk about where things dey.
texts.r:skill:e.e4.read: Find who do wetin and where in di text, then answer.
texts.r:skill:e.e5.gram: Use **an** before vowel sound and **a** before consonant sound. Use **There is** for one thing and **There are** for plenty things.
texts.r:skill:e.e5.comp: To compare two things, use **-er + than**. To say “di most”, use **the -est**. Use **more** with long words.
texts.r:skill:e.e5.future: For wetin you go do, use **will + base verb** or **be going to + base verb**.
texts.r:skill:e.e5.transform: For negative sentences, use **not / don't / doesn't / didn't**. For questions, put **Are / Do / Does** at start of sentence.
texts.r:skill:e.e5.read: Long texts easy if you find who, where, when, and wetin, like say you dey underline dem.
texts.r:skill:e.e6.tense: For something wey dey happen now, use **be + -ing**. For past, use **past tense**. For future, use **will / be going to**.
texts.r:skill:e.e6.modal: After **can** (fit), **must** (must), **should** (e good make you), and **may** (you fit), use base form of verb.
texts.r:skill:e.e6.vocab: Learn similar-meaning words and opposites together to double your vocabulary.
texts.r:skill:e.e6.read: Read text with plenty sentences and find who do something, when dem do am, and why.
texts.r:skill:e.e6.seq1: Order words like **First**, **Then / Next**, **After that**, and **Finally** show di order wey things happen.
texts.r:skill:e.e6.pun1: Sentence start with **capital letter** and end with correct **punctuation mark**: full stop (.) for statement, question mark (?) for question, and exclamation mark (!) for surprise or strong feeling. Always use capital letter for people names and di word I.
texts.r:skill:e.vocab: Learn common words with **sound + meaning + spelling** together to remember dem for long. Tap speaker button to hear how dem sound.
texts.r:skill:e.be: Verb be change form depending on subject. **I → am**, **he / she / it → is**, **you / we / they → are**.
texts.r:skill:e.pres: When subject na **he / she / it (third person singular)**, add **-s / -es** to verb. Words wey end with -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o take -es. For consonant + y, change y to i and add -es!
texts.r:skill:e.plural: For two or more, usually add **-s** to noun. Nouns wey end with -x take **-es**. Learn irregular plurals by heart. Sentence order na **subject → verb → di rest**.
texts.r:skill:e.order: For two or more, usually add **-s** to noun. Nouns wey end with -x take **-es**. Learn irregular plurals by heart. Sentence order na **subject → verb → di rest**.
texts.r:skill:e.m2.perf: Use have/has + past participle. E show experience, completion, or something wey still dey continue. Know di difference between since (starting time) and for (period of time).
texts.r:skill:e.m2.pass: Use be + past participle to say something happen to somebody or something. Add who do am using by.
texts.r:skill:e.m2.inf: Use want, hope, decide + to-infinitive; enjoy, finish, avoid + gerund. Stop + to V show purpose, and stop + V-ing mean stop an action.
texts.r:skill:e.m2.comp: Use -er/-est and more/most. Use than with comparisons and the with superlatives. good → better → best dey irregular.
texts.r:skill:e.m2.read: Read question first, then find di sentence with clue. Title and main idea cover di whole text.
texts.r:skill:e.m2.sum1: To summarize, find di **main idea** and make am short in one or two sentences. Sentence about only one detail, one wey add something wey no dey in passage, or one wey too broad no be good summary.
texts.r:skill:e.m3.rel: Join two sentences into one with who (people), which (things), that (both), and whose (ownership).
texts.r:skill:e.m3.cond: If + present, will + V (something wey fit happen). If + past, would + V (imagine something wey no true now).
texts.r:skill:e.m3.ques: Use order: question word + subject + verb. No use do/does/did.
texts.r:skill:e.m3.part: -ing show active or ongoing action; -ed show passive or completed action. For feelings, use -ing for thing wey cause feeling and -ed for person wey feel am.
texts.r:skill:e.m3.read: Join clues together to make inference. Decide purpose of text by checking its requests and claims.
texts.r:skill:e.h1.tense: Use had + p.p. for something wey happen before another past event. Use have been -ing for action wey continue reach now.
texts.r:skill:e.h1.clause: where / when / why be relative words wey work like adverbs. whether / that dey introduce noun clauses.
texts.r:skill:e.h1.partc: Remove conjunction and subject, then change verb to -ing. Subject must be same for both parts.
texts.r:skill:e.h1.conn: Know di difference between cause and effect (so, therefore), contrast (however), examples (for example), and addition (in addition).
texts.r:skill:e.h1.main: Main idea often dey after However, wey turn common belief around, and for last sentence. Fill blank by following di flow: problem → solution → result.
texts.r:skill:e.h2.inv: When Never/Hardly/Only then come first, order turn to auxiliary + subject. Use It is ~ that to add emphasis.
texts.r:skill:e.h2.subj: For I wish / as if / If clauses, use past tense for opposite of present, and had p.p. for opposite of past.
texts.r:skill:e.h2.wh: whatever, whoever, whichever, and however + adjective mean “no matter what / who / which / how ...”.
texts.r:skill:e.h2.vocab: Guess meaning of new word from contrast, example, and cause clues, and from its prefix.
texts.r:skill:e.h2.logic: Follow text by finding what pointing words refer to and checking linking words. Gather details to reach conclusion.
texts.r:skill:e.h3.par: Phrases wey and/but/or join must have same form. Verb must agree with main subject.
texts.r:skill:e.h3.tone: Use descriptive and emotion words to identify mood. Check whether di text dey ask, inform, or persuade to find its purpose.
texts.r:skill:e.h3.ins: Use linking words, pointing words, and time order as clues to arrange sentences and find where given sentence fit.
texts.r:skill:e.h3.col: Learn word pairs wey dey go together, like make a decision, take a risk, heavy rain. Guess idiom meaning from di situation.
texts.r:skill:e.h3.sum: Find main idea and contrast expressions for di text, then shorten dem to one sentence.
texts.r:skill:e.h.conv: For conversation questions, check not just whether grammar correct but whether tone natural and polite for di situation. Suggestions, interruptions, replies to compliments, idioms, and indirect speech dey show often.
texts.r:skill:e.h.job: For workplace English, main things na idioms (touch base), short forms (ASAP, etc.), and verb-preposition pairs (collocations). No translate word by word; remember phrases as people use dem at work.
texts.r:skill:e.h.media: For media English, e important to separate facts from opinions and judge whether reasoning behind a claim make sense. Learn terms like image descriptions (alt text, caption) and editing tools by wetin dem do.
texts.r:skill:e.h.world: For world-culture topics, learn important words like culture, diversity, stereotype, and phrases for understanding other cultures without judging dem. Use context clues to tell similar-looking words apart.
texts.r:skill:e.h.lit: For literature questions, know wetin each term mean and apply am to scene for story. Keep foreshadowing, symbol, point of view, theme, and character roles separate.
texts.r:skill:e.h.debate: Debate need you to know di difference between terms (motion, rebuttal, etc.), evidence types, and logical fallacies. When you dey evaluate claim, first ask, “Wetin be di evidence for dis?”
texts.r:skill:e.h.write: For writing, choose form wey fit di purpose and reader, then check sentence parts (subject and verb) and logic of linking words. For specific texts like resume, actions and numbers better pass vague words.
